jobs.title: Graduate Transport Planner
jobs.description:
At Curtins, we're an employee-owned engineering consultancy driven by a simple ambition: to create a better built environment for everyone.

For over 65 years, we've delivered practical, innovative and sustainable solutions that make a positive impact on communities across the UK and Ireland. From major regeneration schemes and commercial developments to education, healthcare and residential projects, our work helps shape the places where people live, learn, work and thrive.

As a Graduate Transport Planner, you'll work alongside experienced planners, engineers and consultants, contributing to a wide range of projects while developing the technical and professional skills you need to build your career.

Whether you're interested in transport assessments, active travel & sustainable mobility, highways or public transport, we'll give you the experience, guidance and support to find the areas that interest you most and develop your expertise in development planning.

What you'll be doing

You will support the planning and development process, helping clients bring projects forward from initial concept through to planning approval.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Assisting with the preparation of Transport Assessments and Transport Statements.

  • Supporting the production of Travel Plans and technical planning reports.

  • Analysing traffic, transport and movement data.

  • Assisting with junction assessments and development impact studies.

  • Supporting planning applications for residential, commercial and mixed-use developments.

  • Working alongside planners, civil engineers and other specialists to deliver integrated solutions.

  • Attending client meetings, project discussions and stakeholder consultations.

  • Taking part in wider Curtins activities including STEM outreach, charity initiatives and community projects.

What kind of projects will I get to work on?

You'll be involved in projects across a wide range of sectors, including:

  • Residential developments.

  • Urban regeneration schemes.

  • Commercial and industrial projects.

  • Education and healthcare developments.

  • Mixed-use masterplans.

  • Strategic land and development opportunities.

You'll help assess how developments interact with the transport network and support clients through the planning process, helping turn ideas into deliverable projects.

How will Curtins support my development?

Our goal is simple: to help you become the best engineer you can be.

Through the Curtins Graduate Academy, you'll follow a structured development programme designed to accelerate both your technical and professional growth.

You'll benefit from:

  • A structured graduate development programme.

  • Dedicated mentoring and coaching.

  • Regular technical and professional skills training.

  • Support towards professional registration and Chartership.

  • Exposure to a wide range of projects, clients and sectors.

  • Opportunities to build your network across the business.

You'll be supported by experienced professionals who are genuinely invested in your success and development.

What we're looking for

We're looking for graduates who are curious, analytical and interested in how development projects are planned and delivered.

You'll ideally be studying towards or have recently completed a degree in:

  • Transport Planning

  • Geography

  • Urban Planning

  • Civil Engineering

  • Town Planning

  • Geography or a related discipline

It would also be advantageous to hold an MSc in Transport Planning, Transport Engineering, Urban Planning, or Development Planning.

Most importantly, we're looking for people who share our values:

Integrity - Doing the right thing.

Being Human - Supporting and respecting others.

Curiosity - Asking questions and seeking better solutions.

Impact - Making a meaningful difference through our work.

Why join Curtins?

As an employee-owned business, every person at Curtins contributes to and benefits from our success.

Alongside exciting projects and a supportive culture, you'll enjoy:

  • Industry-leading benefits package.

  • Award-winning training and development programmes.

  • Employee ownership benefits.

  • Opportunities to get involved in STEM, charity and community initiatives.

  • Access to our unique Employee Extras, including our 5-star holiday lodges.

Most importantly, you'll be joining a business where your ideas matter, your development is supported and your contribution makes a real difference.

Build your future with Curtins.

Should you wish to discuss any adjustments to the application process or provide us with feedback please contact hr@curtins.com we would be happy to discuss ways we can make the process more suitable to your needs.

We value diversity and respect all differences in people. We invite enthusiastic individuals who share in our values of teamwork, client focus, integrity, and quality to apply to join us.

jobs.description: We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want. You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models. Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week. How it works Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another. Requirements 2+ years of professional software engineering Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code) Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++ Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing Regular use of an AI coding tool Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words At least 10 hours a week, starting now A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines) Nice to have Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure Experience building agent tasks or RL environments Terms US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer Please mention the word **LEVITY** and tag RMjAuMTY5LjU4LjE= when applying to show you read the job post completely (#RMjAuMTY5LjU4LjE=). We have been running since 2014, and we pioneered deliverability technology such as Inbox rotationâ¢ and deliverability AIâ¢. The Role We are hiring a technical customer support person with an owner's mentality. You will own support for QuickMail and Mailflow, our deliverability add-on. There is no first or second line. You are the first and last person our customers talk to. Customers count on you to solve their problems and find the real cause when something breaks. You work closely with engineering, and you tell the founder what we need to know to make the product better: where the friction is and where the opportunities are. The role covers the help desk, system health checks, testing new releases before they ship, and leading the weekly team meeting. It takes excellent communication, solid technical understanding and sharp critical thinking. This is not a script-reading job. Most tickets involve deliverability, DNS records, LinkedIn automation or campaign setup. You dig into customer accounts in our Support Dashboard, reproduce the issue, then decide what to do and how to explain it to the customer. We are a remote team spread across time zones. Most routine tasks have a written guide with a checklist, so you know what done looks like. You are expected to refine and improve those processes. When something new comes up, you work out the most efficient way to handle it. If you want a lot of autonomy across many areas, real responsibility and a fast-paced environment, this role is for you. What Work Looks Like You own two things: customers get unstuck fast, and the product stays reliable. Every day Set the day's support priorities and work the Help Scout queue for QuickMail and Mailflow. Triage, resolve, and dig deeper when a ticket needs it. Check the support dashboard: job queue, event-stream latency, blacklist status, newly purchased domains. If something is off, investigate, diagnose, and drive it to resolution. Review fraud alerts and disable accounts that are scams or abusing the platform. Delighting customers Comfortable jumping on calls with customers, building rapport fast, and setting them up for success. Update the changelog and help articles based on what shipped and what customers asked. Review its answers, fix the docs it drew from when it is wrong, and contact the customer when its reply was off. Test them, confirm when staging is ready to ship, and think through how existing and new users will be affected. When a core feature breaks (emails not sending, login down), confirm it, alert the team on Slack or Telegram, update the status page every 30 minutes, keep affected customers informed, and drive the fix. Then run the retrospective so it does not happen twice. Running the week Lead the weekly team meeting in MonsterOps: issues written up, to-dos done, numbers updated. Keep rock status and KPIs current in MonsterOps. Tools you'll use: Helpscout, our Support Dashboard, Sidekiq, GitHub, Slack, Telegram, MonsterOps, Outline, MxToolbox, Postmark, Bento, TidyCal, Fathom, Visual Code and Claude. You act with a constant sense of urgency. You can execute fast and find new ways to improve your productivity. You are resourceful. You use all the tools at your disposal to get great results. You have a low ego. You don't take offense easily and you handle disagreement as a discussion, not a personal attack. Growth mindset. You are positive about new workflow/process/product/tool changes. You love giving and receiving positive and negative feedback without getting defensive. Hours that overlap with East coast US and UK, where most of our customers are. A Plus If You Have Experience with customer facing work, or if you don't have it, tell us why you are perfect for this role. Working knowledge of deliverability and LinkedIn outreach. Warmup, DNS, inbox rotation, DKIM, SPF, Outlook and Gmail technical setup. We can teach this, but a head start helps. Comfort with agency setups. Workspaces, guest seats, inbox purchases and what happens when an agency loses a client. Light data skills. You can pull numbers from Help Scout or our MCP to back up what you report. An eye for happy customers. You notice them and ask for testimonials and case studies at the right moment. How We Work Together You'll work directly with the founder and with our lead developer. Direction can change. The founder may say one thing, then something different a few days later as they learn more. When that happens, check what changed and adapt. Information should be short and to the point. Lead with what matters, then give more details if asked. The founder can stay frustrated about a problem until it's solved. That's something they are aware of and working on. You'll do well here if you can stay calm and focused when the pressure is on. Are you studying marketing, communications or business and looking for a student job where you can build hands-on marketing experience and see how it all comes together in practice?

Weâre looking for a structured and proactive Marketing Student Assistant to join our Brand & Marketing team at Copenhagen Optimization.

Youâll work alongside our Head of Marketing, Growth Marketing Manager and Content Strategist, helping us turn plans into action across digital, events, content and campaigns. Itâs a hands-on role with plenty of variety and room to take on more responsibility as you grow.

What you'll work on

  • Website & digital: Update and maintain website content, event and campaign pages, and help keep everything accurate and up to date.

  • Events: Support conferences and events around the world â from registrations and exhibitor portals to materials, print orders, attendee lists and deadlines.

  • Content & campaigns: Support campaign execution by preparing content assets, landing pages, lists and other campaign elements.

  • Marketing coordination: Keep calendars, project pages, assets and plans organized, coordinate smaller deliverables and follow-ups, and help make sure the practical details don't fall between the cracks.

  • Creative support: Help adapt or create simple marketing materials and visuals. Experience with Canva, Figma or similar tools is a plus.

Who we're looking for

You are studying marketing, communications, business or a related field, ideally with at least one or two years of your studies remaining.

You like creating structure, following things through and seeing a task go from idea to done. Youâre dependable, attentive to detail and comfortable taking initiative. We donât expect you to know everything from day one â what matters is that youâre curious, eager to learn and interested in how marketing works in practice.

You:

  • Communicate confidently in English, both written and spoken.

  • Work in a structured way and keep track of tasks and deadlines.

  • Take initiative and care about the quality of what you deliver.

  • Are comfortable working with digital tools. We use HubSpot, Notion, Dropbox and LinkedIn, but you don't need to know them all already.

  • Are interested in marketing and keen to learn across different disciplines.

Who is Copenhagen Optimization?

Copenhagen Optimization is the company behind Better Airport, our software platform built for intelligent airport operations.

We work with airports around the world to connect planning, resource management, staffing and day-of operations, enabling them to make better operational decisions every day.

Founded in Copenhagen in 2014, we have offices in Copenhagen and Boston and customers across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and beyond.

What we offer

Approximately 15â20 hours per week, with flexibility around your studies, exams and personal life. Youâll join a small marketing team, work closely with experienced colleagues across the business and gain hands-on experience in international B2B marketing.

Weâre looking for someone who wants to stay with us for the longer term, become part of the team and gradually take on more responsibility.

Interested?

Send us your application and CV and tell us a little about yourself, why this role interests you and what you think you'd bring to the team.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and may fill the position once we've found the right person.

jobs.title: Senior Level Designer
jobs.description:
Blackbird Interactive is a creative-fueled, future-driven, independent game studio where the best talent in the industry can find long-term careers to help grow their abilities while working on a wide range of projects, which encompass world-class IPs as well as our own creations across multiple genres. Our studio operates as a remote-first workplace, offering flexible work arrangements. PLEASE NOTE: At this time, we are only able to hire candidates who are legally eligible to work in Canada and reside within Canada. Blackbird Interactive is looking for an experienced Senior Level Designer to help build and deliver high-quality gameplay spaces for an action RPG focused on fast-paced combat, character progression, exploration, and replayability. This role focuses on designing levels, encounters, and environments that create satisfying combat opportunities, reward exploration, and support a wide variety of player builds and abilities. You'll work closely with systems design, combat design, art, narrative, audio, and engineering to create spaces that complement the game's core combat systems while providing strong pacing, readability, and a sense of discovery. The role involves collaborating with leadership to align content with the overall creative vision while owning levels end-to-end, from initial layout and blockout through implementation, iteration, and polish. As a senior designer, you'll be expected to independently solve complex level design problems, provide strong design judgment, and help establish a high quality bar for playable content across the game. 
 Responsibilities Collaborate with combat, systems, narrative, art, engineering, audio, and production to create levels that support the established creative vision and core gameplay pillars Own levels end-to-end, including layouts, blockouts, combat spaces, encounters, traversal, exploration, pacing, and player flow Design engaging combat spaces that support varied enemies, character builds, abilities, positioning, and different approaches to combat Create rewarding exploration through optional paths, secrets, environmental storytelling, and meaningful rewards while maintaining clear navigation and progression Script and implement gameplay events, encounters, objectives, triggers, and environmental interactions directly in engine Test, debug, and iterate on levels using playtest feedback to improve combat flow, difficulty, pacing, readability, and replayability Requirements A minimum of 8 years of game development experience, with significant experience designing and implementing levels for action, RPG, or combat focused games Experience shipping multiple titles, including at least one in a senior or equivalent level design role Proven ability to independently own complex levels from initial concept and blockout through implementation, iteration, and final polish Strong understanding of action RPG level design, including combat spaces, encounter pacing, exploration, progression, player guidance, and replayability Strong hands-on experience with level editing, gameplay scripting, and in-engine implementation, with the ability to prototype, debug, and iterate quickly Strong design judgment, communication, and collaboration skills, with the ability to balance gameplay quality, creative goals, technical constraints, and production realities Pluses Passion for action RPGs centered on combat, character builds, loot, progression, and exploration Experience designing levels for an isometric or elevated gameplay camera, with an understanding of its impact on combat readability, navigation, and composition Experience creating replayable content that supports different character builds, abilities, difficulty levels, or repeated playthroughs Appreciation for systemic combat and how level geometry, enemy composition, hazards, and interactive elements combine to create varied encounters Experience designing dungeons, interconnected environments, procedural or modular level content, or other repeatable gameplay spaces Strong instincts for environmental storytelling, gameplay readability, polish, and identifying opportunities to improve the player experience through iteration 
 $115,000 - $149,500 a year

·       Develop project plans for client onboarding and standardization projects, outlining tasks, resources required, and estimated timelines

 

·       Install, configure, diagnose, test and resolve technical hardware and software issues

·       Provide mentorship and guidance to Tier I and Tier II service desk technicians, fostering a collaborative and knowledgeable team environment

 

·       Contribute to the development and improvement of IT service management processes and practices

 

·       Evaluate and anticipate IT trends and recommend strategies and implement improvement initiatives

·       Helpdesk / Ticketing – HaloPSA

 

·       Documentation – Hudu

 

·       RMM – Intune / Immybot

 

·       Networking – Meraki

 

·       Email/Calendar/Voice/AD – Microsoft 365

 

·       Security Cameras – Rhombus / Avigilon

 

·       Door Access – Avigilon

 

Qualification

 

·       6+ years of experience providing IT services and end-user support

 

·       Prior experience at a managed service provider is critical to understand the fast-paced nature of the industry

 

·       Client-oriented approach with a passion for delivering high-quality customer service

 

·       Proven experience leading IT projects

 

·       A self-starter who is eager to expand their qualifications

 

·       Background in providing direct end-user support

 

·       High level of attention to detail

 

·       Excellent verbal and written communication skills

 

·       IT-related degree and/or certifications (Cisco, A+, Network+, Microsoft, or equivalent)

Dream Big, Then Make it Real

 

We flex our imagination and challenge ourselves to a higher standard.  Do, rather than talk and tell.

 

Client Driven Results

 

Clients trust us to find solutions that deliver exceptional results.  When they succeed, we succeed.

 

Own Your Progress

 

We continuously improve through rapid innovation and embracing our mistakes.  Own it means a relentless pursuit of the solution.

 

We Do It Right…even when no one’s watching. Period.

We are looking for an independent, flexible, remote opportunity where you can help improve AI-powered search technology from the comfort of your home? If you're curious, internet-savvy, and enjoy evaluating online content, this freelance project could be a great fit.

 

A Day in the Life of a Content Reviewer - US

In this role, you will analyze and provide feedback on text, webpages, images, and other types of online content for leading search engines using a specialized online platform.

 

By reviewing and rating search results for relevance and quality, you will help improve the overall search experience for millions of users around the world, including yourself.

Join our global community and put your skills to work supporting one of the world's leading search technologies.

 

Service Rates 

The rate of pay is $0.2333 per completed task, with an estimated earning potential of $14 per hour. Compensation is based on tasks completed and project availability. Estimated earnings may vary depending on task volume and program requirements including, quality, and productivity, in accordance with the program's quality standards and guidelines.

 

Please note that only one member per household may participate in this program. If it is identified that more than one person from the same household is participating in the TELUS Digital Rating Program, all associated accounts may be removed from the program.

 

Independent Contractor Relationship

This opportunity is offered on an independent contractor basis. Contributors have the flexibility to choose when and how much they work, subject to project availability and quality requirements. This opportunity is not and should not be construed as creating an employment relationship with TELUS Digital.

 

Qualification path

Qualification Process

No previous professional experience is required to apply for this opportunity. However, participation in this project requires meeting the basic requirements and successfully completing the qualification process.

 

Basic Requirements

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English

• Must have resided in the United States for the past three consecutive years

• Familiarity with current and historical business, media, sports, news, social media, and cultural affairs in the United States

• Active use of Gmail and social media platforms

• Experience using web browsers to navigate and interact with a variety of online content

• Daily access to a reliable broadband internet connection

• Access to a smartphone (Android 5.0 or higher, or iOS 14 or higher)

• Access to a personal computer

 

Assessment

You must complete an English language assessment, pass an open book qualification exam, and complete an ID verification in order to be successful for this role. These assessments will determine your suitability for the position.

In this role, you’ll work across a variety of client projects to find cost-effective, high-quality, and pragmatic solutions to complex e-commerce challenges. Responsibilities will include:

  • Collaborating closely with Technical Leads and Designers to meet clients' custom e-commerce and technical needs.
  • Building and maintaining high-performance storefronts using both custom Liquid (Online Store 2.0) and modern headless architectures (Shopify Storefront API, GraphQL, Hydrogen/Remix, Next.js).
  • Implementing responsive, accessible, and pixel-perfect interfaces based on design specifications, with meticulous attention to product interaction details and motion design.
  • Integrating custom storefronts with headless CMS platforms (Sanity, Contentful), payment gateways, subscriptions, search, and third-party e-commerce APIs.
  • Optimizing e-commerce performance, focusing heavily on Core Web Vitals, image/video asset delivery, bundle size, and runtime efficiency across high-traffic collection and product pages.
  • Architecting scalable, reusable component libraries and design systems tailored for commercial platforms.

We’re always pitching for new and exciting technology niches. Some of the areas below are relevant to us!

  • 8+ years writing highly performant frontend code with an obsession for 95+ Lighthouse scores and optimal Core Web Vitals.
  • Deep Shopify Ecosystem Mastery: Proven experience building custom Shopify themes (Liquid, JSON templates, Online Store 2.0) as well as headless storefronts using the Shopify Storefront API (GraphQL) and frameworks like Hydrogen/Remix or Next.js.

  • Architecture & State Management: Experience with state management solutions (Zustand, Redux, Pinia) and API integration patterns for cart state, multi-currency, and checkout flows.
  • Quality & Accessibility: Experience building accessible (WCAG compliant), responsive interfaces with a strong commitment to SEO best practices, testing frameworks (Jest, Playwright, Cypress), and maintainable code.

We prefer long standing relationships with highly accountable and communicative team members, so we encourage candidates to expect longer term engagements.

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

Our AML Investigations team is crucial in this mission and is responsible for detecting suspicious activity, conducting thorough investigations, and shutting down bad actors. This team is growing and we’re looking to hire an additional AML Risk Investigator to help us with Bank Partner Requests for Information, Transaction Monitoring, Financial Crime Investigations, Case Management and drafting Unusual Activity Reports. You’ll need to learn how a really wide range of businesses work and bring your knowledge to bear on our processes and product. jobs.description: Headquarters: Remote, United States Principal Product Manager, Agentic AI REMOTE, United States JOB OVERVIEW Legion is building AI agents that carry out workforce management work, not agents that describe it. Much of what is presented as AI in workforce management today is a conversational layer over an existing scheduling screen. The more substantial problem — software that reasons over demand, labor regulation, and employee preferences, then acts, with a person in the loop wherever the stakes require one — remains unsolved across the category. Legion intends to solve it, and this role leads the product work to get there. You will take an agent surface from operational research through specification, prototype, evaluation, and enterprise deployment, working hands-on throughout. You will work closely with Legion's AI Lab engineers and with our CEO, who is engaged in this work daily. RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES Agent definition. Determine what an agent is responsible for, which tools it may call, what it must escalate, what it must never do, and what a manager sees when it acts. These decisions affect employee pay and legal compliance. Much of this work is pre-launch, so you will shape the direction rather than inherit it. Problem selection. The hardest judgment in agentic product work is identifying which workflows suit an agent and which do not. You will spend substantial time inside customer operations — district managers, store managers, labor operations, frontline employees — and return with a ranked, defensible view of where an agent creates measurable value and where it does not. The human-in-the-loop contract. Scheduling decisions affect income, childcare arrangements, and legal protections. For each agent action you will define where autonomy is appropriate, the escalation thresholds, how a manager overrides the system, what is logged, and how a compliance team audits the outcome. Legion treats this as a first-class design problem. Build quality. You are accountable for what ships, not for what was specified. That means staying engaged through implementation: reviewing the build against the specification as it comes together, using the product yourself before anyone else is asked to, joining bug triage and design review, catching drift from intent while it is still cheap to correct, and holding a release when the quality is not there. Our customers experience the build, not the document. A well-written specification that produced a product managers do not trust is failed product work, and we assess it that way. Evaluation. Build and maintain the evaluation sets that determine whether an agent is ready to ship and whether it is degrading in production — writing the cases, reviewing failure traces, setting the pass criteria. You will be the person who holds a release when the demonstration is persuasive and the evaluation is not. Specifications. Legion uses Functional Requirements Documents as its ground-truth specification layer; release notes, enablement material, and sales content are generated from maintained specifications rather than reconstructed from code or institutional memory. Write FRDs that meet that standard and keep them accurate after release. A specification is where the work begins, not where your responsibility ends. Commercialization. Partner with go-to-market on packaging, metering, pricing inputs, and field readiness. Agentic products raise difficult commercial questions — what unit to meter, what a customer is paying for when software performs work a person previously did — and you will be expected to hold a considered position on them. Design-partner delivery. Lead agent deployments with large enterprise design partners: scoping the pilot, establishing success criteria before it begins, joining failure reviews, and determining what becomes generally available and what remains bespoke. TECHNICAL EXPECTATIONS Legion is looking for a product manager who builds, rather than one who directs others who build. In a typical week, this role involves: Writing and iterating on prompts and system prompts directly, and explaining why a change improved a behavior Standing up a working prototype of a proposed agent — tool definitions, structured outputs, retries, guardrails — before engineering is asked to build anything Using agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent) daily: prototyping, data analysis, specification work, and reading the codebase behind your specifications Reviewing an execution trace and diagnosing whether a failure originates in a tool description, a retrieval gap, a context-window constraint, an under-specified output schema, or a genuine model limitation Building and running evaluation sets, and interpreting the results without a data scientist to translate them Holding an informed position on retrieval design, tool-use patterns, structured output, model routing, latency and cost trade-offs, and multi-tenant safety in enterprise SaaS Opening pull requests against our codebase — a prototype, a prompt change, an evaluation fixture, a specification stub. Pushing code is permitted and actively encouraged for product managers who want to work that way. It is not a requirement of the role, and the same review standards apply to everyone. Following model releases, agent frameworks, and protocol changes, and translating them into roadmap implications within days rather than quarters We recognize that this is a demanding technical bar for a product role. It reflects what the work actually requires. REQUIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS 7+ years in product management (Senior) or 10+ years (Principal), including at least 2 years shipping LLM-backed features to external, paying users — not internal tools, proofs of concept, or hackathon projects Demonstrated hands-on capability of the kind described above. Expect to show your work. Substantial enterprise B2B SaaS experience: multi-tenant architecture, role-based access control, audit trails, single sign-on, data residency, security review, and enterprise procurement. You should be able to anticipate what a customer's security questionnaire will ask about an LLM feature. A record of taking an ambiguous, operationally complex domain problem through to a shipped product with demonstrated adoption — not only launch Evidence of staying with a product through implementation and owning its quality at release. We will ask about a release you delayed or stopped, what you found, and how you found it. The judgment to recognize what current models cannot do reliably, and the willingness to say so when a room expects a different answer Comfort working inside a codebase. An engineering background is not required, but you should be able to read the code behind what you are specifying, run it locally, and open a pull request. Strong written communication. Legion runs on documents, and candidates are evaluated substantially on how they write. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS AND ATTRIBUTES Direct experience in workforce management, HCM, ERP, supply chain, or another operationally complex enterprise domain with compliance exposure Familiarity with labor compliance regimes — predictive scheduling ordinances, meal and rest break rules, union work rules — or demonstrated ability to become fluent in a comparable regulatory domain quickly Background in demand forecasting, optimization, or decision systems Experience building platform or authoring surfaces that customers configure themselves An engineering or technical degree, or prior experience as an engineer or data scientist Experience with products sold into frontline-heavy industries: retail, hospitality, healthcare, or manufacturing SCOPE OF ROLE, STATED PLAINLY So that candidates can assess fit early: This is an individual contributor role. There is no team to inherit and no management responsibility at present. The role is accountable for what ships, not for what is specified. Writing the specification is a portion of the work, not the whole of it. This is not an AI strategy or vendor-evaluation role. The work is product definition, prototyping, specification, evaluation, and delivery. The role requires forming an independent point of view from operational research. Direction will not be handed down in detail. The environment carries genuine ambiguity. The category is being defined as we work in it, and model capabilities shift underneath the roadmap. SELECTION PROCESS Our process includes a practical exercise: a sanitized workforce management problem, for which candidates produce an agent design — scope, tools, failure modes, human-in-the-loop contract, and evaluation plan — together with a working prototype they built themselves, using any model provider they prefer. The exercise is then discussed with the people the candidate would work alongside. We weigh it heavily, and we compensate candidates for the time. COMPENSATION & BENEFITS Salary Range: $280,000-$300,000 +bonus (tied to business outcomes) +Stock Equity At Legion, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to all employees. As a fully remote employer, pay for positions is determined using local, national, and industry-specific survey data. Our posted salary range is done so in good faith based on national data and may be refined for a candidate's region/town/cost of living. We strive to make competitive offers that allow employees room for future growth. Salaries will be based on the applicant’s location, level of experience, education, and specialized knowledge and skills. Additionally, we consider the external market rate, the amount we have budgeted internally, and the internal equity for the same position within the company. Headquarters: Remote, United States

Principal Product Manager, Agentic AI

REMOTE, United States

JOB OVERVIEW

Legion is building AI agents that carry out workforce management work, not agents that describe it.

Much of what is presented as AI in workforce management today is a conversational layer over an existing scheduling screen. The more substantial problem — software that reasons over demand, labor regulation, and employee preferences, then acts, with a person in the loop wherever the stakes require one — remains unsolved across the category. Legion intends to solve it, and this role leads the product work to get there.

You will take an agent surface from operational research through specification, prototype, evaluation, and enterprise deployment, working hands-on throughout. You will work closely with Legion's AI Lab engineers and with our CEO, who is engaged in this work daily.

 

RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES

Agent definition. Determine what an agent is responsible for, which tools it may call, what it must escalate, what it must never do, and what a manager sees when it acts. These decisions affect employee pay and legal compliance. Much of this work is pre-launch, so you will shape the direction rather than inherit it. 

Problem selection. The hardest judgment in agentic product work is identifying which workflows suit an agent and which do not. You will spend substantial time inside customer operations — district managers, store managers, labor operations, frontline employees — and return with a ranked, defensible view of where an agent creates measurable value and where it does not.

The human-in-the-loop contract. Scheduling decisions affect income, childcare arrangements, and legal protections. For each agent action you will define where autonomy is appropriate, the escalation thresholds, how a manager overrides the system, what is logged, and how a compliance team audits the outcome. Legion treats this as a first-class design problem.

Build quality. You are accountable for what ships, not for what was specified. That means staying engaged through implementation: reviewing the build against the specification as it comes together, using the product yourself before anyone else is asked to, joining bug triage and design review, catching drift from intent while it is still cheap to correct, and holding a release when the quality is not there. Our customers experience the build, not the document. A well-written specification that produced a product managers do not trust is failed product work, and we assess it that way.

Evaluation. Build and maintain the evaluation sets that determine whether an agent is ready to ship and whether it is degrading in production — writing the cases, reviewing failure traces, setting the pass criteria. You will be the person who holds a release when the demonstration is persuasive and the evaluation is not.

Specifications. Legion uses Functional Requirements Documents as its ground-truth specification layer; release notes, enablement material, and sales content are generated from maintained specifications rather than reconstructed from code or institutional memory. Write FRDs that meet that standard and keep them accurate after release. A specification is where the work begins, not where your responsibility ends.

Commercialization. Partner with go-to-market on packaging, metering, pricing inputs, and field readiness. Agentic products raise difficult commercial questions — what unit to meter, what a customer is paying for when software performs work a person previously did — and you will be expected to hold a considered position on them.

Design-partner delivery. Lead agent deployments with large enterprise design partners: scoping the pilot, establishing success criteria before it begins, joining failure reviews, and determining what becomes generally available and what remains bespoke.

TECHNICAL EXPECTATIONS

Legion is looking for a product manager who builds, rather than one who directs others who build. In a typical week, this role involves:

  • Writing and iterating on prompts and system prompts directly, and explaining why a change improved a behavior
  • Standing up a working prototype of a proposed agent — tool definitions, structured outputs, retries, guardrails — before engineering is asked to build anything
  • Using agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent) daily: prototyping, data analysis, specification work, and reading the codebase behind your specifications
  • Reviewing an execution trace and diagnosing whether a failure originates in a tool description, a retrieval gap, a context-window constraint, an under-specified output schema, or a genuine model limitation
  • Building and running evaluation sets, and interpreting the results without a data scientist to translate them
  • Holding an informed position on retrieval design, tool-use patterns, structured output, model routing, latency and cost trade-offs, and multi-tenant safety in enterprise SaaS
  • Opening pull requests against our codebase — a prototype, a prompt change, an evaluation fixture, a specification stub. Pushing code is permitted and actively encouraged for product managers who want to work that way. It is not a requirement of the role, and the same review standards apply to everyone.
  • Following model releases, agent frameworks, and protocol changes, and translating them into roadmap implications within days rather than quarters

We recognize that this is a demanding technical bar for a product role. It reflects what the work actually requires.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • 7+ years in product management (Senior) or 10+ years (Principal), including at least 2 years shipping LLM-backed features to external, paying users — not internal tools, proofs of concept, or hackathon projects
  • Demonstrated hands-on capability of the kind described above. Expect to show your work.
  • Substantial enterprise B2B SaaS experience: multi-tenant architecture, role-based access control, audit trails, single sign-on, data residency, security review, and enterprise procurement. You should be able to anticipate what a customer's security questionnaire will ask about an LLM feature.
  • A record of taking an ambiguous, operationally complex domain problem through to a shipped product with demonstrated adoption — not only launch
  • Evidence of staying with a product through implementation and owning its quality at release. We will ask about a release you delayed or stopped, what you found, and how you found it.
  • The judgment to recognize what current models cannot do reliably, and the willingness to say so when a room expects a different answer
  • Comfort working inside a codebase. An engineering background is not required, but you should be able to read the code behind what you are specifying, run it locally, and open a pull request.
  • Strong written communication. Legion runs on documents, and candidates are evaluated substantially on how they write.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS AND ATTRIBUTES

  • Direct experience in workforce management, HCM, ERP, supply chain, or another operationally complex enterprise domain with compliance exposure
  • Familiarity with labor compliance regimes — predictive scheduling ordinances, meal and rest break rules, union work rules — or demonstrated ability to become fluent in a comparable regulatory domain quickly
  • Background in demand forecasting, optimization, or decision systems
  • Experience building platform or authoring surfaces that customers configure themselves
  • An engineering or technical degree, or prior experience as an engineer or data scientist
  • Experience with products sold into frontline-heavy industries: retail, hospitality, healthcare, or manufacturing

SCOPE OF ROLE, STATED PLAINLY

So that candidates can assess fit early:

  • This is an individual contributor role. There is no team to inherit and no management responsibility at present.
  • The role is accountable for what ships, not for what is specified. Writing the specification is a portion of the work, not the whole of it.
  • This is not an AI strategy or vendor-evaluation role. The work is product definition, prototyping, specification, evaluation, and delivery.
  • The role requires forming an independent point of view from operational research. Direction will not be handed down in detail.
  • The environment carries genuine ambiguity. The category is being defined as we work in it, and model capabilities shift underneath the roadmap.

SELECTION PROCESS 

Our process includes a practical exercise: a sanitized workforce management problem, for which candidates produce an agent design — scope, tools, failure modes, human-in-the-loop contract, and evaluation plan — together with a working prototype they built themselves, using any model provider they prefer. The exercise is then discussed with the people the candidate would work alongside. We weigh it heavily, and we compensate candidates for the time.

 

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Salary Range: $280,000-$300,000 +bonus (tied to business outcomes) +Stock Equity

At Legion, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to all employees. As a fully remote employer, pay for positions is determined using local, national, and industry-specific survey data. 

Our posted salary range is done so in good faith based on national data and may be refined for a candidate's region/town/cost of living. We strive to make competitive offers that allow employees room for future growth. Salaries will be based on the applicant’s location, level of experience, education, and specialized knowledge and skills. Additionally, we consider the external market rate, the amount we have budgeted internally, and the internal equity for the same position within the company. 

Benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • $0 monthly premium and other flexible medical, dental, and vision plans effective on the first day of employment
  • 401k plan
  • Discretionary Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays
  • Parental Leave 
  • Equity 
  • Monthly Wellness Reimbursement
  • Monthly Lunch on Legion

ABOUT LEGION

Join Legion's mission to turn hourly jobs into good jobs. We're a remote, mission-driven team seeking exceptional talent to propel this vision. Embrace a culture that's collaborative, fast-paced, and entrepreneurial. With us, you'll grow your skills, work closely with experienced executives, and contribute significantly to our mission.

If you're ready to make an impact and grow your career, Legion is where you belong. Join us in making hourly work rewarding and fulfilling.

We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.

Sanctuary Computer - Development

At Sanctuary Computer we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.

Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.

XXIX - Design

garden3d TK — Media

At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.

We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.

Plus, our partner organizations

Lightphone
Mill
IngredientAI

⛰️ The Head of Technology Role

The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder & president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.

You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.

This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.

This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.

They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.

They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.

Responsibilities & Mandates

️ Systems that hold up

We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.

All in on agentic development

The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.

Practical engineering

We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value engineering: the simplest thing that works, built well, at a cost the client is glad to pay.

Code quality at Sanctuary Computer

Sanctuary Computer is where our engineering standard lives, so this is where most of their energy goes. They set what good code review looks like, keep our senior developers sharp on architecture and quality, and make sure that bar holds without slowing the team down.

Hiring and empowering the very best

They are a magnet for exceptional engineers. They know where to find them, how to convince them, and how to give them enough room to do their best work while still holding them to the standard. People who work for this person should get visibly better, and should say so.

Estimation, scoping and delivery

They make sure our teams can reliably estimate and story point the work ahead, and that we deliver at a pace that meets the dates we promised and protects our margins. When an estimate is wrong, they find out why and fix the process.

The technical voice in new business

Our clients include Google, Stripe, Figma, Mozilla and The Nobel Prize. This person joins new business calls as the trusted technical consultant, scopes the work, writes the technical side of proposals, and can explain a hard tradeoff to a client's CTO and their CEO in the same meeting.

Hardware sense

We're the software team behind The Light Phone and Mill, so a good share of our work touches devices. This person doesn't need to be a firmware engineer, but they understand how hardware works, where it constrains the software, and how to plan a project that spans both.

The garden3d technology story

Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.

Culture

They model garden3d's values of partnership, curiosity, and accountability. The engineers they lead do the best work of their careers here, because the feedback is honest, the recognition is earned, and the craft rubs off

 Special Projects

In addition to day to day responsibilities, here’s an idea of some of the projects this role may spearhead or support in coming years →

  • Making agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer builds, with loops and evals the whole team trusts
  • Setting the shared technical conventions every garden3d studio builds from
  • Landing the kind of flagship engineering engagement that changes what people think we do
  • Hiring the next generation of the engineering team, across every garden3d studio
  • Turning the internal tools and agents we build for ourselves into products
  • Partnering with the Head of Design so our own studio websites are as well engineered as they are designed

Qualifications

This is a great opportunity for someone looking to make a significant impact in a growing, dynamic company. Based on the responsibilities of this role, we think the right candidate has the following experience and skills:

Must have:

  • 12+ years building software, at least three of them leading engineers inside a studio, agency, startup or founder-led company
  • Deep experience engineering complex systems, shipped and run in production: distributed services, data pipelines, multi-platform products
  • A true technology generalist, comfortable across frontend, backend, data, infrastructure and native
  • A strong preference for practical engineering: convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms as a service over bespoke infrastructure
  • All in on agentic development: loop engineering, evals, and agents doing real work in a real codebase
  • Fluency across most of our stack: React, Next.js, Ruby on Rails, Elixir & Phoenix, Sanity, Postgres, Redis. You won't use all of it every week, but you should be able to review any of it
  • Experience as the technical lead in winning work: scoping, estimating and pitching to clients
  • A track record of hiring exceptional engineers, and of people who got measurably better working for them
  • Hands-on. This person can still write the code, not only review it (and will get on the tools when the need arises)

Nice-to-have:

  • A sense of how hardware works: firmware, embedded systems, IoT, and shipping software for physical products
  • Experience in a client services environment (a consultancy, agency or studio)
  • Experience in a Sales Engineer or Solutions Architect role
  • Open source projects they've started or maintained
  • Experience fostering close collaboration between design and engineering teams
  • Experience inside a worker-owned, open-book, or otherwise unusual company
  • A network in the engineering community: the meetups, the conferences, the people worth hiring
  • Interests in design, art, music, food or fashion. We find these people have a well rounded sense of quality

Who you are

The person we’re looking for is happy, relaxed and easy to get along with and appreciates a commitment to a culture of transparency, non-dictatorial leadership styles, and alternative methodologies. They’re flexible on anything except conceits that will lower their usually outstanding work quality. They work “smart” by carefully managing their workflow and team.

How we interview

After you submit your application, a member of our team will reach out. Our interview process starts with an intro call to answer any questions you have about the role and to learn a bit more about your experience and interests.

From there, we’ll follow up with a panel interview call where you get to meet a few members of our team, to openly discuss some of our challenges and ensure your skills and interests align with where we’re going as a business.

For qualified candidates, the process wraps with a reference call, and an offer to follow.

Compensation

This is a permanent leadership role. If this individual exceeds expectations in their first four months, we'll shape the permanent role together, with scope and compensation that grow as the studios and their revenue do. After a period of proven success (12 - 24 months), they become eligible to join our worker ownership program.

We start with a 4-month fraction trial contract, paid hourly between $110 - $175 p/hr pending seniority & experience. In the first few weeks of the trial, this individual will propose their own goals to define success in their trial, and present them to our leadership team for approval.

At garden3d, we believe that those who shoulder the most responsibility and create the greatest impact should be paid accordingly. This role greatly favors autonomous, competent & ambitious operators.

‍ How we work:

We believe that there’s a better balance between the poles of freelancing & full time, and for that reason we work differently to most shops:

  • Transparency & Ownership: We release out Profit & Loss statements to the community each year, open source our best ideas, and talk business & money with everyone in the company. We’re proud to run our business with integrity, and for that reason we share everything with our team & community.
  • 150% Carbon Negative: Our studio offsets 150% of the carbon we use to do business each year, dated back to our founding in 2015. We turn down work that is not in-line with our morals, and we encourage our peers to do the same. We have been certified climate neutral since 2021.
  • Strong Morals: Since our founding, we've turned down somewhere between $1mm - $2mm of work that didn't meet our moral standards. (Most of that was DTC brands that can't show a valid sustainability initiative).
  • Async & Decentralized: We use tools optimized for calm, thoughtful communication, and opt for async whenever possible. We fight hard to maintain our focus time.
  • Remote Friendly: Our company is fluent in remote work, making our workplace more decentralized, and democratized in the process.
  • Ideas & Products: In our spare studio time, we work to build our own open source or internal products to diversify & bolster our income. We create amazing technology products for our clients, so why not for the studio?

→ Read more on our Substack, over here.

How to apply

We’re excited to hear from you! ❤

Kindly submit a complete and thoughtful application, including relevant links that help verify your work experience and identity. Applications with missing or insufficient information will not move forward in the review process.

Our team carefully reviews every complete submission, and we truly appreciate the time and effort you put into applying! :)

Headquarters: Bulgaria
URL: http://jobhire.ai

Description

CVM Lead (US Market)

Location: Remote

Job Type: Full-time

About JobHire.AI

JobHire.AI is a vertical AI agent that automates job search for professionals in the US market. We find, tailor, and apply to jobs on behalf of thousands of paying subscribers — at scale and with precision. We operate a subscription model with monthly and longer-term tiers, plus paid add-ons. We're entering a phase where deeper customer value management — not just acquisition — is the single biggest unlock for profitable growth.

Why This Role Now

We are spending efficiently to acquire users — but a substantial portion of revenue is left on the table after the first purchase. Reg→Purchase conversion is below where it should be. Rebill rates erode quickly past month one. Add-on attach is minimal. Our reactivation engine is currently offline. We've been operating an email-only CRM on a platform that doesn't return analytics through its API.

That ends with this hire. This is a role for someone who has already done the transformation we need: turning a basic broadcast CRM into a measurable CVM function that drives incremental revenue across email, SMS, and web push — on the US market specifically.

What You'll Own

Funnel Conversion

  • Drive Reg→Purchase conversion through triggered post-quiz, paywall-abandonment, and onboarding sequences across email, SMS, and web push.
  • Own first-purchase activation across the first 7 days.

Retention & Rebill

  • Differentiate renewal sequences by plan tier (1 / 3 / 6 month).
  • Build pre-cancel intervention flows — pause offer, plan-switch, value reminder — using captured cancel reason.
  • Move the dial on month-1 rebill rate, the single most leveraged metric in our subscription economics.

Reactivation

  • Build the reactivation engine for the cancelled cohort — across email and SMS, personalized by cancel reason and tenure.
  • Recover revenue from a base that is currently dormant due to deliverability issues.

Add-on Monetization

  • Own the CRM-driven path to add-on products (Resume Review, Resume Builder): timing, segmentation, copy, channel.

Channel & Tooling

  • Lead the migration off our current ESP onto our chosen omnichannel platform (Maestra is the current candidate; Customer.io is the alternative).
  • Recover and maintain email domain reputation.
  • Stand up SMS as a first-class channel — including US compliance (TCPA, A2P 10DLC).
  • Stand up web push and orchestrate cross-channel flows (email → SMS → push cascades).

Measurement

  • Implement incremental measurement with holdouts on every flow. We don't want activity reports — we want incremental revenue, attributable and defensible.

Expected Outcomes

First 3 Months

  1. Email deliverability restored to historical baseline.
  2. Reactivation campaign launched with measurable incremental conversion against a holdout.
  3. Differentiated renewal flows live for 1 / 3 / 6 month plans.
  4. Decision (signed off with engineering) on omnichannel platform: migrate to Maestra or alternative.

First 6 Months

  1. SMS and web push live as ongoing production channels in lifecycle flows.
  2. Measurable lift in Reg→Purchase conversion via paywall-abandonment and post-registration triggered sequences.
  3. Measurable lift in month-1 rebill rate via differentiated and intervention flows.
  4. Add-on attach rate (Resume Review, Resume Builder) materially up via CRM-driven sales sequences.
  5. Per-flow incremental revenue reported weekly via proper holdout methodology.

12 Months

  1. CVM channel contributing as a top-3 incremental revenue source for the company.
  2. Cross-channel lifecycle strategy (email + SMS + web push + iMessage/RCS as those channels mature in the US) live and documented.
  3. Process documentation and tooling stable enough to remove key-person risk.


We keep our hiring process quick and simple:

  • HR Introduction Call
  • Team Interviews
  • Challenge
  • Reference Check (with three prior managers)


Requirements

You're a Fit If You Have

  • 3+ years operating CVM/lifecycle programs on the US market specifically. US b2c subscription. This is non-negotiable — US deliverability, US carriers, US consumer behavior, US compliance.
  • 5+ years total in CRM / lifecycle / CVM, with at least one stint owning the function end-to-end (not just executing).
  • Hands-on operating experience with an enterprise omnichannel platform — Maestra strongly preferred; Braze, Iterable, Customer.io, or Klaviyo also relevant.
  • Real, hands-on experience launching SMS as a marketing channel in the US (TCPA, A2P 10DLC, carrier compliance — not "I worked with a vendor who handled it").
  • Real, hands-on experience launching web push and measuring its lift.
  • SQL good enough to pull your own segments and validate your own data.
  • A subscription-business orientation: you think in LTV/payer, payback period, retention curves, and cohorts — not in opens and clicks.
  • A track record of measurable incremental revenue from CRM, ideally validated through holdout.
  • Bias toward action. We operate as a tiny team; you'll need to ship faster than you plan.

Nice to Have

  • Experience migrating off a damaged email domain.
  • Experience in job search, career, HR-tech, or adjacent consumer subscription verticals (EdTech, FinTech, dating, streaming).
  • iMessage Business / RCS experience.
  • Communication (speak English and Russian).


Benefits

  • Clear mandate and ownership from day one. You're the function, not a contributor to it.
  • The economics are highly leveraged — even a 5-percentage-point lift on month-1 rebill is meaningful to the bottom line of the company.
  • Direct work with the CMO, CEO, and Growth PM. No layers, no politics.
  • A market where your work is directly visible to users searching for their next job — outcomes you can feel.
  • $4000-7000/month + 38DaysOff.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/jobhire-crm-cvm-lifecycle-retention-marketing-lead-us-b2c-subscription-only

jobs.title: Développeur(-euse) Expérience IA (IA conversationnelle)
jobs.description: Headquarters: Canada (Remote) Upgrade aide ses clients à avancer dans la bonne direction grâce à des produits financiers abordables et responsables. Depuis 2017, nous avons aidé plus de 7,5 millions de clients à accéder à plus de 42 milliards de dollars en crédit à la consommation. En nous concentrant sans relâche sur l'amélioration du bien-être financier de nos clients, nous développons des produits qui leur permettent de faire des économies et qui les soutiennent pour un meilleur avenir financier. Nous sommes soutenus par certains des meilleurs investisseurs dans le domaine de la technologie et avons été récemment valorisés à 7,3 milliards de dollars. Nous sommes constamment reconnus pour notre culture de collaboration et d'inclusion. Plus récemment, nous avons été classés parmi les Premières entreprises fintech au monde par CNBC, Meilleurs lieux de travail par Built In, et par le San Francisco Business Times, Meilleurs lieux de travail d'Amérique par Newsweek, Meilleur employeur ''Startup'' par Forbes, et Employeurs les plus sains par Phoenix Business Journal. Nous recherchons de nouveaux membres d'équipe qui sont enthousiastes à l'idée de concevoir et de proposer des produits nouveaux et meilleurs. Rejoignez-nous et aidez à bâtir un meilleur avenir financier pour des millions de personnes. À propos du rôle Un(e) Développeur(-euse) Expérience IA est responsable du cycle de vie complet des parcours que nos clients vivent avec l'agent IA d'Upgrade par clavardage, par téléphone et par courriel : création, optimisation, gestion des cas particuliers et augmentation du taux de résolution autonome. Cette personne conçoit des parcours dans les outils sans code de Sierra, collabore avec les groupes produits d'Upgrade pour intégrer leurs processus de service à l'agent, et répond de la capacité de l'agent à résoudre le problème du client de façon sécuritaire, exacte et sans intervention humaine. Nous recherchons un(e) Développeur(-euse) Expérience IA pour prendre en charge l'agent IA d'Upgrade destiné à la clientèle. Vous ferez le lien entre les équipes de développement, de produit et des opérations clientèle. Vous transformerez des processus de service, comme effectuer un paiement, consulter les détails d'un prêt, mettre à jour une adresse ou activer les paiements préautorisés, en parcours de production, et vous continuerez à les améliorer après leur lancement. Vous concevrez et gérerez les parcours de A à Z, de la première ébauche jusqu'à leur pleine maturité. Le travail est à la fois celui d'un bâtisseur et d'un analyste : concevoir le parcours, gérer les cas particuliers, lire les transcriptions et augmenter continuellement le taux de résolution autonome. Le taux de résolution autonome, la satisfaction client (CSAT), la qualité des transferts et le taux d'hallucination sont vos indicateurs clés. Au cours de votre première année, vous serez responsable d'un portefeuille de parcours couvrant l'ensemble de nos produits (prêts personnels, carte, paiement différé (BNPL), marge de crédit hypothécaire (HELOC), dépôts) et contribuerez à établir les normes selon lesquelles Upgrade conçoit, teste et déploie ses expériences IA. Nos technologies principales Sierra Agent Studio (parcours sans code), simulations et analyse des conversations Sierra, API GraphQL et REST (comme outils de parcours), Genesys (transfert vers le centre de contact), SumoLogic, Grafana, SQL, JavaScript/TypeScript, Claude et autres outils de LLM. Ce que vous ferez Création de parcours : Concevoir et développer des parcours Sierra dans Agent Studio pour le clavardage, la voix et le courriel, de la phase de découverte avec les opérations jusqu'au déploiement en production Optimisation : Analyser chaque semaine les transcriptions, les enregistrements et les données analytiques, repérer où les conversations échouent ou sont transférées, et déployer des correctifs à la logique des parcours, aux instructions et à la base de connaissances Gestion des cas particuliers : Cartographier les scénarios problématiques (paiements refusés, identité non concordante, comptes en souffrance, demandes non prises en charge) et s'assurer que chacun se conclut par une réponse exacte ou un transfert fluide Résolution autonome : Assumer la responsabilité des cibles de résolution autonome et de CSAT pour chaque parcours, mener des déploiements progressifs (1 % → 100 %) et prioriser les travaux ayant le plus d'impact sur ces indicateurs Partenariat produit : Collaborer avec les groupes produits (prêts personnels, carte, BNPL, dépôts) pour définir la portée de nouveaux parcours, maintenir les parcours à jour au fil de l'évolution des produits et définir les API dont l'agent a besoin Sécurité et conformité : Appliquer l'authentification à plusieurs niveaux et la vérification renforcée, le libellé de conformité exact ainsi que des garde-fous contre les hallucinations et les réponses non conformes aux politiques Transferts : Concevoir les transferts vers des agents humains dans Genesys avec des résumés exacts et le contexte d'authentification Tests : Créer des suites de simulation et de tests de régression afin que chaque modification de parcours soit déployée avec la preuve qu'elle n'altère pas le comportement existant Surveillance : Suivre la latence, les erreurs et les abandons dans SumoLogic et Grafana, et être responsable des alertes Optimisation vocale : Latence, phrases de transition, interruptions, personnalité et ton Relation avec Sierra : Agir à titre de responsable technique de notre côté, faire remonter les problèmes liés à la plateforme et orienter les demandes relatives à la feuille de route Ce que nous recherchons De 3 à 5 ans d'expérience en développement logiciel, ou une expérience équivalente dans des rôles en solutions techniques, en IA conversationnelle ou en gestion de produits techniques Connaissance pratique du comportement des agents LLM : instructions, appels d'outils, récupération de connaissances, et les points de défaillance de chacun Expérience dans la conception d'évaluations pour des systèmes non déterministes : jeux de tests, simulations, LLM évaluateur (LLM-as-judge), seuils de régression Une maîtrise technique suffisante pour lire des spécifications d'API, collaborer avec des développeurs backend sur des intégrations REST et GraphQL, et raisonner sur les autorisations et les portées de permissions Un esprit axé sur le produit et le client : vous comprenez les procédures opérationnelles, lisez les transcriptions, accordez de l'importance au ton et mesurez votre réussite selon la résolution du problème du client Sens des responsabilités en production : déploiements, surveillance, analyse de journaux et réponse aux incidents Rédaction claire et capacité à travailler avec des interlocuteurs non techniques des équipes des opérations, de la conformité et des affaires juridiques Atouts supplémentaires Expérience pratique de Sierra Agent Studio ou d'une plateforme d'agents sans code comparable (Decagon, Ada, Kore.ai, Google CCAI, Amazon Lex/Connect) Expérience en IA vocale : reconnaissance vocale (speech-to-text), synthèse vocale (text-to-speech), optimisation de la latence, gestion des interruptions (barge-in) Connaissance des systèmes de centre de contact tels que Genesys et de la conception de transferts vers des agents Expérience en fintech ou dans un autre secteur réglementé (UDAAP, FDCPA, TCPA, PCI, SOC 2) Expérience en conception conversationnelle ou en rédaction UX Ce que nous vous offrons Salaire compétitif ($140K-$180K) et plan d'options d'achat d'actions Assurances médicales, dentaires et de la vue payées par l'entreprise Congés payés flexibles Possibilités de croissance et de développement professionnel Congé parental payé Initiatives de santé et de bien-être Exigence linguistique English language is required for this position, as it involves interacting with staff at Upgrade's offices worldwide. L'anglais est requis pour ce poste, puisqu'il comporte des interactions avec le personnel des bureaux d'Upgrade à l'échelle internationale. Conditions environnementales et de travail Le travail s'effectue à l'intérieur dans un environnement au rythme soutenu qui exige la capacité de gérer plusieurs priorités et de respecter les processus de travail, les horaires et les attentes en matière de service établi. Les employés saisissent, extraient et échangent régulièrement des informations avec précision à l'aide de systèmes et d'applications numériques afin d'appuyer les objectifs opérationnels et de service à la clientèle. Le poste exige la capacité de recevoir et d'échanger des informations avec les clients, les collègues, les superviseurs et les partenaires interfonctionnels par le biais des moyens de communication disponibles, qui peuvent inclure des réunions, des courriels, des appels téléphoniques et des outils de collaboration numériques, et peut impliquer des échanges en temps réel, verbaux ou en personne selon les besoins de l'entreprise. Les fonctions peuvent inclure la gestion d'un volume élevé d'interactions entrantes et/ou sortantes avec la clientèle ainsi que d'activités de travail à l'aide de systèmes de télécommunication et informatiques. Le poste exige la capacité de lire, d'analyser et d'interpréter les informations affichées à l'écran d'ordinateur et de maintenir une posture de travail pendant de longues périodes, conformément aux exigences du poste. Le travail peut s'effectuer dans un centre de contact, un bureau ou en télétravail, selon les besoins de l'entreprise et la nature du poste. Les environnements de travail sur place peuvent inclure des espaces de travail partagés, un éclairage de bureau standard et un bruit de fond modéré typique des environnements de service à la clientèle ou opérationnels. Les employés en télétravail sont responsables de maintenir un espace de travail sécurisé et productif avec une connexion Internet fiable qui prend en charge les systèmes de l'entreprise et protège la confidentialité des informations de l'entreprise et des clients. Des mesures d'adaptation raisonnables peuvent être mises en place pour permettre aux personnes qualifiées vivant avec un handicap d'exercer les fonctions essentielles du poste, conformément à l'Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) et aux lois étatiques et locales applicables. Nous sommes un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances et nous valorisons la diversité au sein de notre entreprise. Nous ne faisons pas de discrimination fondée sur la race, la religion, la couleur, l'origine nationale, le sexe, l'orientation sexuelle, l'âge, l'état civil, le statut d'ancien combattant ou le statut de handicap. Upgrade n'accepte pas les candidatures spontanées soumises par des agences de recrutement, des cabinets de recherche de personnel ou toute autre tierce partie. Tout CV soumis à un employé d'Upgrade sans accord écrit préalable en vigueur sera considéré comme la propriété d'Upgrade, et Upgrade ne sera pas tenue de payer des bonus de recommandation ou de placement. Les agences doivent obtenir une approbation écrite au préalable du service d'acquisition de talents d'Upgrade pour soumettre des candidatures, et ce, seulement si une entente valide et dûment signée est en vigueur. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/upgrade-developpeur-euse-experience-ia-ia-conversationnelle

You'll thrive here if you think about the health of the whole program, enjoy improving how work gets done, and are equally comfortable digging into a detailed case and having a direct conversation with a customer about acceptable use.

Empathy and curiosity: You approach every customer with patience and a desire to dig deeper, especially when a conversation gets uncomfortable.

Clarity: You explain complex technical concepts simply and help others do the same.

Collaboration: You build strong partnerships across Support, Customer Success, and Engineering, and you treat customer outcomes as a shared goal.

Thinking at scale: You look at how we do things today and see what could work better for the whole organization, then you help make it happen.

Continuous learning: You stay ahead of evolving standards and see change as a chance to improve how we work.

  2. Rest of World (ROW; which is comprised of 9 different languages)

The Senior Quality Lead will break down silos within the Quality organization, establish a unified operating model, and leverage AI-powered tools to scale quality insights. 3. Legal Basis
